From: Elena Morales <elena@zephyrwellness.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@zephyrwellness.com>

Subject: Data processing asks for pilot (no-training + EU-only)

Hi David,

Thanks for the demo last week — the latency profile looked good for our summaries pilot. Before we sign a pilot SOW, Legal and Procurement have a few non-negotiable asks we need on record:

- A clear no-training commitment for any customer content used in production (we can't allow model updates or fine-tuning on our data).
- Processing limited to EU-based infrastructure for the pilot (data residency requirement).
- A complete list of subprocessors with roles and locations.
- Evidence you can provide operational proof (SFTP export or on-demand audit logs) to show data residency and access control.

Attached is a spreadsheet with the redlines Procurement will propose — mostly DPA items. Can you confirm whether Redwood can commit to an EU-only processing lane for Zephyr and provide the subprocessor inventory + a short ops runbook showing how you will segregate their data?

If this is doable, Procurement will move forward with a short SOW. Thanks — Elena

[Attachment: zephyr_dpa_questions.xlsx (xlsx)]

Elena — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: yes, we can support an operational EU-only processing lane for a pilot and provide a no-training commitment for customer production interactions. A few clarifying points and next steps: 

1) No-training commitment: we can contractually commit not to use Zephyr production content to update or fine-tune models used to serve your tenant. We typically scope this to "production inference logs and stored customer interactions." We will surface precise wording legal needs to sign.

2) Subprocessors and evidence: I attached our current subprocessor inventory CSV (sanitized) and can provide an ops runbook showing routing rules that pin requests to EU regions (GCP eu-west1 for this pilot). For extra assurance we can enable an SFTP export of session logs to Zephyr's SFTP endpoint on demand.

3) Telemetry and ephemeral logs: the only potential exception is ephemeral telemetry used for telemetry/health (latency/error metrics) — we can either exclude Zephyr from this telemetry or ensure it is aggregated and non-identifiable. I'll loop in Privacy to confirm the operational approach.

Next steps: I'll get Karthik to propose precise contract language for the DPA no-train clause, and Marissa will propose a commercial attachment for the reserved pilot lane and any pricing delta. Can we aim for a draft DPA/redline by Wednesday?

Best,
David

[Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_v2.csv (csv)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Elena Morales <elena@zephyrwellness.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data processing asks for pilot (no-training + EU-only) — proposed DPA language

Elena / team — following up from Privacy. Draft guidance on contract language and operational limits below. I'll schedule a short call if you want to walk through.

- No-training clause (proposed): "Redwood shall not use Customer Content submitted in production inference requests to train, fine-tune, or improve models used in production to serve Customer. Customer Content shall not be included in any datasets for model training absent Customer's prior written consent."

- Scope note: We recommend explicitly defining "Customer Content" to include user inputs, prompt exchanges, and any derived outputs from the tenant's production environment. We should be careful to exclude system health telemetry (e.g., per-request latencies) which we can agree to either exclude entirely or to aggregate and retain in a privacy-preserving manner.

- Subprocessors: the provided CSV lists current subprocessors and their roles. For Zephyr's DPA we can include an SLA that requires 30 days' notice before adding any new subprocessor that has access to tenant data; for critical subprocessors we can offer prior written notice + opportunity to object.

- Evidence: Operational proofs we can provide: (1) signed subprocessor list snapshot, (2) routing configuration export showing egress to eu-west1 for the tenant, (3) SFTP session export of session logs on request (48-hour export SLA). We can also provide a SOC2 report and a short onshore routing architectural diagram.

Open items for your Procurement team to confirm: whether the SFTP export cadence and retention windows are acceptable, and whether they require on-prem KMS for key custody. If Zephyr needs on-prem KMS, that's a different Private deployment path and has longer lead time.

I'll attach a short DPA markup with the wording above in the next email.

—Karthik
